title: Grading Every Man Utd Player’s 2026–27 So Far As Mauricio Pochettino Takes Over
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Ewan Ross-Murray4:00 PM ESTMan Utd have endured a dismal start to the current campaign. / James Gill/Danehouse/Getty Images (Martínez & Tielemans), Marc Atkins/Getty Images (Fernandes)Manchester United’s miserable start to the current campaign has finally seen Michael Carrick succumb to the axe.

The vultures circling overhead had only grown in numbers since an utterly dismal opening day defeat to newly promoted Hull City, and that was merely the first in a series of embarrassing capitulations under the 45-year-old’s guidance.

Mauricio Pochettino has been selected as Carrick’s successor, but the former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea manager inherits a beleaguered squad bereft of self-belief. Their subpar performances were the catalyst for United’s latest managerial change.
Pochettino has the unenviable assignment of raising morale and standards, but the opening 15 matches of the 2026–27 campaign have left little room for optimism.
Perhaps this is the perfect juncture at which to asses the performances of United’s players.

Senne Lammens has struggled in his second season. / Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesAppearances: 14Clean Sheets: 1Goals Conceded: 27After an encouraging debut season between the sticks, Senne Lammens’s form has fallen off a cliff. The costly mistake he made for Belgium at the summer’s World Cup has seemingly undermined his confidence, and Carrick’s final match, the chaotic 4–4 draw with Aston Villa, spotlighted his struggles as he gifted the Villans their second of the match. The only mitigating factor for the 24-year-old is just how desperate the defense ahead of him has been.

The summer recruit, signed on a free transfer as Lammens’s deputy, has only played once for his new employers, yet it was a competitive debut to forget. Darlow produced an uninspiring display as United surrendered a two-goal lead during their Carabao Cup exit at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion.

Diogo Dalot has been dreadful. /  Carl Recine/Getty ImagesApps: 14Clean Sheets: 0Goals Conceded: 26Goal Contributions: 0There’s simply no world in which United can blossom into a serious soccer side with Diogo Dalot at fullback. It’s astonishing that the Portuguese defender is still an automatic starter considering his generally unspectacular and often erratic displays during his eight years—yes, really—at Old Trafford. Carrick’s defense conceded 26 goals while Dalot was on the field this term, and their only clean sheet came with him out of the side.

Harry Maguire has a very specific skillset. When things are going well, his bulky frame and aerial prowess are handy assets, but he’s not an individual capable of rescuing a misfiring backline singlehandedly. When things are going badly, his lack of mobility and clunky technique can look rather amateurish.

Leny Yoro’s start to the season has epitomized his time in Manchester. The 21-year-old has struggled to adapt to the speed and ferocity of the Premier League, and his shortcomings have been evident throughout displays at right back and center back this term. Perhaps Pochettino can nurture the Frenchman, but things look rather bleak for him nearly two-and-a-half years into his United career.

Lisandro Martínez has been a liability on and off the field. / Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA Images/Getty ImagesAppearances: 11Clean Sheets: 1Goals Conceded: 11Goal Contributions: 1Lisandro Martínez’s three most noteworthy contributions this season have all been negative. First, there was his remarkably comical own goal in the draw with Fulham in September. Next, the defender publicly lambasted club chief Jason Wilcox, piling unnecessary pressure on Carrick and the club at a difficult moment. Finally, he was idiotically sent off in the 2–0 defeat to Chelsea on Halloween, which only served to cast further doubt over his future with United.

Noussair Mazraoui is certainly not an elite fullback capable of elevating United to higher standards, but the Morocco international remains a generally safe pair of hands. He’s absolutely unspectacular—which is exactly what United require right now—and certainly not the most pressing issue in an abysmal defense which ranks as the second-worst in Europe’s top five leagues.

Ayden Heaven deserves sympathy having been drafted into the United dumpster fire as an inexperienced 20-year-old, but his individual performances in the heart of defense have hardly inspired confidence. There’s a talented player in there, though.

Injuries have been an issue for Luke Shaw once again. / Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty ImagesApps: 5Clean Sheets: 0Goals Conceded: 6Goal Contributions: 1The injury-prone left back was surprisingly healthy throughout last season, but he’s spent much of the current campaign back in the treatment room. Shaw has made just five appearances, and while he was hardly setting the world alight before his latest fitness issue, United are undoubtedly a stronger side when he’s in their starting lineup.

It feels harsh to judge Matthijs de Ligt this early in his recovery. The Dutchman made his first start in 11 months as United were thrashed 4–1 by Como, and he looked understandably rusty as the Italians tore his defense to shreds. Still, his performance must be viewed in the proper context, and he will have plenty of shots at redemption as he returns to full fitness.

Despite Shaw’s injury issues, Carrick refused to trust academy talent Harry Amass. Two brief cameos from the bench in the Champions League are all he’s been given this season, but he can at least boast zero goals conceded during his 29 minutes on the field. Silver linings, eh?

Bruno Fernandes’s standards have dropped. / Ed Sykes/Sportsphoto/Allstar/Getty ImagesAppearances: 14Goals: 6Assists: 3Carrick was so heavily reliant on Bruno Fernandes’s sorcery during his interim spell, but the skipper’s outstanding creative numbers were never sustainable. Nine goal involvements this season isn’t bad, and his hat trick against Ipswich Town was excellent, but United would have still expected much more from the 32-year-old. They wouldn’t, however, have anticipated his criticism of Carrick after the defeat to Como, which reeked of unprofessionalism.

There was nothing but plaudits for United after their opportunistic addition of Youri Tielemans in the summer. After all, the midfielder was integral to Aston Villa’s ascent under Unai Emery, and appeared set to add another touch of class to United’s engine room. However, his mobility issues have been brutally exposed early in his United career, as has inability to perform without an out-and-out ball-winner alongside him.

United’s midfield remains an absolute mess, but Kobbie Mainoo can’t be blamed. The academy graduate was crucial to Carrick’s interim success and has continued to deliver relatively consistent showings this season, too. Mainoo just needs a defensively-minded partner to elevate his game, as evidenced by his terrific double act with Casemiro.
